recognize_zh: 右側嗜中性球細胞質內有兩顆與主核完全分離、圓形深紫的小包涵體（黑箭頭，Howell-Jolly body-like inclusion）；左側細胞核葉上的小附屬物（紅箭頭）與核相連，屬 Barr body。兩細胞並有毒性顆粒（toxic granulation）。
features: Two neutrophils with abundant cytoplasm containing coarse, dark toxic granules
Right neutrophil: small round, dense basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions completely separate from the nucleus (Howell-Jolly body-like inclusions, black arrows)
Left neutrophil: small nuclear appendage attached to a lobe (Barr body-type appendage, red arrow)
Coarsely condensed nuclear chromatin with hypolobated/band-like nuclear contour in right cell
Background red cells with central refractile drying artifact
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows neutrophils with toxic granulation. One neutrophil contains small, round, deeply basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions that are completely separate from the nucleus and resemble erythrocytic Howell-Jolly bodies (black arrows). The adjacent neutrophil shows a small appendage attached to a nuclear lobe, representing a sex-chromatin (Barr body-type) appendage (red arrow) rather than a free inclusion. Red cells show refractile drying artifact. Findings are consistent with Howell-Jolly body-like inclusions in neutrophils with toxic change, here associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

ddx.vs: Döhle bodies are pale blue-grey, irregular, peripheral cytoplasmic patches of rough ER, whereas HJBLIs are small, dense, round, dark purple nuclear-type fragments.
Morulae are larger, stippled mulberry-like clusters of organisms rather than single homogeneous round dense dots.
MYH9-related inclusions are larger, pale blue, spindle-shaped Döhle-like bodies accompanied by giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
A drumstick is attached to a nuclear lobe by a thin chromatin strand, whereas HJBLIs lie free in the cytoplasm.
